requirement:
After a rejection under {cite}`requirements.authoring.line_numbers.rejection`,
a submission whose previously flagged rationale is exactly the UUID that rejection gave MUST
resolve to the rejected submission unchanged, ignoring the new submission's
other fields; acceptance remains subject to
{cite}`requirements.authoring.submission.searches.line_numbers`. After passing that gate, any other rationale that cites line numbers MUST fail
the assessment, so
an assessment rejects at most one submission. The UUID MUST NOT be recorded in
evidence.
rationale:
Add an end-to-end CLI test in `tests/authoring_cli.rs`, marked `{test}`requirements.authoring.line_numbers.resubmission``. Script it as follows: (1) the model submits a rationale that cites line numbers, and the harness rejects it. (2) The model submits a different rationale that also cites line numbers and is not the UUID. Assert that the assessment fails: the CLI exits unsuccessfully, no evidence is recorded, and the failure message says the rationale cited line numbers after a rejection. Also add a variant where a search is still outstanding at step (2). Assert that the submission is rejected for the outstanding search and does not fail the assessment, and that the rationale correction stays available, so a later exact-UUID resubmission is accepted once the search is finished. — Reviewed tests cover the following. The exact UUID restores the rejected submission and ignores other fields: `src/authoring/line_numbers.rs#mod[tests]/fn[a_rejection_gives_a_uuid_that_keeps_the_rejected_submission]`, `src/authoring/line_numbers.rs#mod[tests]/fn[uuid_restores_only_at_the_rejected_correction_position]`. A UUID with a trailing space and a UUID at the wrong correction position are not accepted: same unit tests. The CLI test `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[keeping_a_rejected_rationale_waits_for_search_and_preserves_the_original_verdict]` covers acceptance staying subject to the outstanding-search gate, the original verdict being preserved, and the UUID not being recorded in evidence.

Two parts of the obligation "After passing that gate, any other rationale that cites line numbers MUST fail the assessment" are not checked:

1. The unit tests only assert that `Rejection::decide` returns `Outcome::Fail`. Nothing exercises the path from a second line-number-citing submission to the assessment actually failing. In `src/authoring/sdk.rs#impl[Review<'_>]/fn[ask]`, the vetting closure maps `Fail` to an error. A regression there would turn the failure into a retry or an acceptance, and the reviewed tests would still pass.
2. The "after passing that gate" ordering is only tested for the exact-UUID resubmission. No test submits a different, non-UUID rationale that cites line numbers while a search is outstanding. The text requires that submission to be handled by the search gate and not to fail the assessment. A regression that fails the assessment before checking outstanding searches would be accepted by the reviewed tests.

The other obligations are adequately tested.

text: :::{req} line_numbers.resubmission
After a rejection under {cite}`requirements.authoring.line_numbers.rejection`,
a submission whose previously flagged rationale is exactly the UUID that rejection gave MUST
resolve to the rejected submission unchanged, ignoring the new submission's
other fields; acceptance remains subject to
{cite}`requirements.authoring.submission.searches.line_numbers`. After passing that gate, any other rationale that cites line numbers MUST fail
the assessment, so
an assessment rejects at most one submission. The UUID MUST NOT be recorded in
evidence.
:::{req} line_numbers.rejection
For requirement, example, and site reviews, when the only submission in a response
under {cite}`requirements.authoring.submission` is otherwise valid but any of its
rationales cites line numbers under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.line_numbers.detection`, and it is the
assessment's first such submission, and it passes the outstanding-search gate
under {cite}`requirements.authoring.submission.searches.line_numbers`, the
harness MUST reject it instead of
accepting it and continue the conversation. The tool result MUST quote the
matched text, identify the affected rationale (including its correction position
for `Failed`), repeat the location guidance of
{cite}`requirements.authoring.judgment_rules`, and give a fresh random UUID,
saying the model may submit once more, either without line numbers or with
the offending rationale set to exactly that UUID to keep the rejected submission as it was.
A rejection MUST be counted in usage like any other turn.
:::{req} submission.searches.line_numbers

The SDK checks for outstanding searches before invoking Habeas's rationale vetting. A submission rejected for an outstanding search MUST leave the rationale correction attempt available under {cite}`requirements.authoring.line_numbers.rejection`.

output.rationale:
`requirements.authoring.line_numbers.resubmission` states only observable behavior. It names no library, algorithm, signature, type, field or named interface that the implementation must use. I checked each clause for a structural obligation:

- "a submission whose previously flagged rationale is exactly the UUID that rejection gave MUST resolve to the rejected submission unchanged, ignoring the new submission's other fields". This describes the outcome. The harness could keep the rejected submission in a map, a field or a closure, or re-parse it, and the result would be the same. How the match is made is discretionary.
- "acceptance remains subject to `requirements.authoring.submission.searches.line_numbers`". This is a cited ordering constraint on behavior, and the cited requirement states it. It prescribes no particular delegation or interface.
- "any other rationale that cites line numbers MUST fail the assessment, so an assessment rejects at most one submission". This is an outcome. The harness could implement it with a counter, a boolean or a state machine.
- "The UUID MUST NOT be recorded in evidence". This restricts what the output contains. It does not prescribe how the output is built.

The cited requirements `requirements.authoring.line_numbers.rejection` and `requirements.authoring.submission.searches.line_numbers` give context only. They are also behavioral, and the task does not ask me to judge them. There are no implementation roots and no acknowledgments, and none is needed. Behavioral evidence from tests falls under the behavioral criterion, not this one.
